pr_body:
fixes #20065 
related #11806 #12493 #18645

I populate `Rearmable` with `Repairable`s logic. Now actors can exist with either having just 1 of the 2 traits or both. When an actor has both traits `Rearmable` is turned off similarly to how `Aircraft` does it, so all collisions are handled in `Repairable`

test cases: 

- add `-Repairable` to `MNLY` and minelayer will still be able to rearm
- change `RearmActors` on `MNLY` to something else and minelayer will still be able to rearm at service depot

issue_context.title: Ground units cannot rearm without `Repairable:` trait
issue_context.body:
For a ground unit to rearm it also needs to be repairable from the same structure. Without `Repairable:` trait the rearm cursor won't even show up.

Easy reproduction case: add `-Repairable:` to minelayer
comments: It appears ground unit rearming logic is coded is in `Repairable` and Aircraft in `ReturnToBase`. It feels very out of place for ground units as one might want units to be able to rearm without having `Repairable`

review_comments: Why not handle rearm-able only here? For backwards compability? All actors that currenty do not have the trait rearmable?
Consider letting other traits call a method in this class that handle rearming. So that all rearm logic is in one place.

I'm thinking of reworking this pr to add an abstract class that both `Rearmable` and `Repairable` inherit from, perhaps `Aircraft` too. It would contain the shared logic and be called something like `ReturnToBase` or as in the comments `DockManager`. Or perhaps a `ReturnToBase` trait instead?

 But I'm still not sure how best to handle collisions.
Similar. If allowed to enter to rearm, then return true already.
I define cursor properties in `Rearmable` as well, It would be best to use them here when you can rearm but not repair at a structure. I'm just not sure exactly how
Or perhaps it would be best to move the cursors to an entirely different trait
